text:
alejandro: Quick FYI — ran a seeded perf sweep across L4/T4/A10 vs A100/H100 and saw a clear divergence in kernel paths around seqlen 48-128. L4/T4/A10 are falling back to slower matmul+attn kernels for a lot of short/medium sequences. heatmap attached (short summary below).

mira: Ugh, saw the same on a customer workload. seqlen 64 conversational bursts drop throughput ~18-22% on L4 compared to the expected preset. Looks like the selector picks a non-fused attn for that range.

jon: Can you paste the reproducer and perf numbers? Also, what batch sizes? smallbatch hysteresis could be flipping the path.

alejandro: Reproducer (very small):
```
model: gpt-medium
seqlen: [8, 16, 32, 64, 128]
batch: 1..16
device_families: [l4, t4, a10, a100, h100]
mode: inference-only, kv-cache enabled
```
Rough numbers (tokens/s, normalized):
- L4 seqlen64 b=4: 1.0 (baseline)
- L4 seqlen64 b=8: 0.92 (mode switch)
- A100 seqlen64 b=8: 1.28
- H100 seqlen64 b=8: 1.33
- A10 seqlen64 b=8: 0.95

mira: Also saw increased memcpy counts on A10 when falling back — KV cache hotpath seems to force copies instead of pointer-sharing in that kernel. Log snippet: 
```
KV_COPY_COUNT=42 per request at seqlen=64
KV_PTR_SHARES=0
```
Not huge on A100/H100.

sarah: @alejandro could this be the autotuner scoring function biasing for peak single-thread flops (which favors a100 kernels) instead of actual end-to-end latency for small batches? Seen regressions when our cost model weights flops too much.

jon: Yeah weight function probably tuned on A100/H100. Two quick mitigations: 1) add device_family multiplier in score, 2) make seqlen bucket thresholds device-aware. Example heuristic: if device in [l4,t4,a10] and seqlen<=96 -> prefer fused-attn-k1; else keep current.

lin: Proposed routing table snippet: 
```json
{"rules": [
  {"device_family": "l4,t4,a10", "seqlen_max": 96, "preferred_kernel": "fused_attn_k1", "max_batch": 8},
  {"device_family": "a100,h100", "seqlen_max": 512, "preferred_kernel": "fused_attn_k2", "max_batch": 64}
]}
```
This reduces the path flips and keeps kv pointers intact for L4/A10.

alejandro: Nice. I also sketched an autotune job that sweeps (seqlen, batch) per device_family and emits a heatmap of kernel choice + tokens/s. We can use that to auto-generate the routing table rules. Want to commit as a nightly job.

mira: Please include KV-copy probe in the autotune so we can penalize kernels that force copies. Add metric: kv_copy_bytes_per_token and memcpy_count.

perf-bot: autotune/job/489 scheduled. CI artifact: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/489/heatmap-l4-a10-a100-h100. Metrics: tokens_s, p99_latency_ms, kv_copy_bytes.

alejandro: Action items: 1) @jon update selector to include device_family multiplier + kv_copy penalty (PR draft by EOD). 2) @lin implement temporary routing table rule for seqlen<=96 on L4/T4/A10. 3) @mira add kv probes to autotune job. 4) Run nightly autotune and review heatmap next week.

sarah: One more note — watch quantized kernel choices on A10, some q8 kernels look faster on A10 but break kv-pointer sharing; add that to the penalty list.

jon: Will do. I'll add a lightweight canary test that runs seqlen=8/64/256 with kv enabled on each family after selector changes.

alejandro: Great. Thanks all, this should reduce the cross-device surprise for PLG users. :thumbsup:
